title: Western Blotting of Hypothalamic Proteins
author: Kira V. Derkach
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xqpfmvn
materials: Keep homogenate on ice for 30 min. 00:30:00

steps.title: Homogenize Hypothalamus Tissue
steps.instruction: Homogenize half of the hypothalamus tissue in 1X Tissue Lysis Buffer at a 1:10 ratio.

steps.title: Clarify Homogenate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 14,000g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to a new tube
Discard the pellet

steps.title: Prepare Protein Samples
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration and prepare samples for loading.

substeps.instruction: Remove 3x3 μl of supernatant to measure protein concentration using the modified Lowry method
Mix an aliquot of lysate containing 300 μg of protein with Lysis Buffer to reach a volume of 50 μl
Add 50 μl of 2X SDS Sample Loading Buffer

steps.title: Denature and Centrifuge Samples
steps.instruction: Heat and cool samples before final centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Warm samples for 5 min at 95 °C
Cool at room temperature for 5 min
Centrifuge samples for 5 minutes using a Microfuge 22R centrifuge (Beckman Coulter, USA)

steps.title: Load Gel and Run Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Load samples into a 1.5 mm thick gel and run electrophoresis using SDS Running Buffer.

substeps.instruction: Load up to 10 μl of sample per well
Select gel percentage based on protein size: 8.5% for 80-200 kDa or 9-14% for 20-65 kDa
Set initial running conditions at 75 V, gradually increasing to 95 V

steps.title: Transfer Proteins to Membrane
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose membrane at 100 V for 1 hour using Transfer Buffer.

steps.title: Block the Membrane
steps.instruction: Prepare the membrane for antibody incubation.

substeps.instruction: Disassemble the transfer sandwich and remove the blotted membrane
Wash the membrane 3-4 times with distilled water
Place membrane in Blocking Buffer (5% non-fat dry milk/TBST) and incubate for 30 min to 1 hour at room temperature with agitation

steps.title: Primary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with primary antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Dilute primary antibody according to manufacturer's recommendations (typically 1:1000 in 5% BSA/TBS-T)
Place membrane in primary antibody solution and incubate overnight at 4°C with agitation

steps.title: Wash After Primary Antibody
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane three times with TBS containing 0.1% Tween-20, 5 minutes per wash.

steps.title: Secondary Antibody Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with HRP-conjugated secondary antibodies diluted 1:1000–1:5000 in 5% non-fat dry milk/TBS-T for 1 hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Final Membrane Washes
steps.instruction: Perform a series of final washes to remove unbound antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Wash 3 times for 5 minutes each with TBS containing 0.1% Tween-20
Wash 2 times for 5 minutes each with TBS without Tween-20

steps.title: Develop and Image Blot
steps.instruction: Detect proteins using ECL and X-ray film.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the membrane (protein side up) with 10 ml of ECL substrate for 1 min (final volume required: 0.125 mL/cm²)
Drain excess detection reagent, wrap the blots, and smooth out air bubbles
Place wrapped blots (protein side up) in an X-ray film cassette and expose to X-ray film for 5 seconds to 60 minutes
